mainTopic: How רבנן and רבי יהודה read the פסוק of גיד הנשה, and the משנה about a גיד הנשה cooked or roasted with other food
overview: The amud first finishes the dispute about eating a small גיד הנשה. רבי יהודה requires a כזית because the פסוק says 'eating', while רבנן use that word to teach that one כזית out of a big nerve is enough. Going back and forth, the גמרא shows how each side uses 'על כף הירך' and 'הירך' differently. It ends that part by answering that the word כף is written twice, so it can both exclude birds and teach שמואל's rule. Then a new משנה teaches that a thigh cooked with its גיד הנשה is forbidden if the nerve gives off taste, measured like meat flavoring a turnip. The same rule applies to a forbidden piece cooked with other pieces: if it is recognized we go by taste, if not all the pieces are forbidden, and the broth always goes by taste. In the גמרא, שמואל limits the משנה to cooking, saying a thigh roasted with the nerve may be peeled and eaten up to the nerve. The גמרא challenges him from רב הונא, who forbids a kid roasted with its חלב even at the tip of its ear, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source: the Torah says 'eating'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires a כזית because the Torah uses the word 'eating' for the גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? 'Eating' is written regarding it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה says you need a full כזית to be liable. The Torah uses the word 'eating' about the גיד הנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Torah law, a real act of 'eating' means eating at least a כזית. So once the Torah says 'eating', a whole nerve smaller than a כזית does not count. רבנן disagree, because they treat the whole nerve as a complete item that counts even when it is small.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating; a halachic 'eating' is normally at least a כזית
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids us to eat
An olive-size amount, the standard minimum for eating

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? 'Eating' is written regarding it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the earlier explanation of רבנן's view and now gives רבי יהודה's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the word אכילה means liability requires at least a כזית.

steps.title: How רבנן use the word 'eating'
steps.stepSummary: רבנן use 'eating' to teach that eating one כזית out of a large nerve makes you liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? That 'eating' teaches that if the nerve has four or five כזיתים and he ate one כזית, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with the word 'eating'. It answers that they use it for a different case: a big nerve where only part was eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this word, one might think you are liable only for eating the whole nerve, since that is what makes it a complete item. 'Eating' teaches that even one כזית out of a large nerve is enough. So רבנן also accept the כזית idea, but only for a partial piece.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That word 'eating' is needed

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אִית בֵּיהּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה זֵיתִים
phrases.english: to teach that when it contains four or five olive-bulks
and he ate one olive-bulk, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבנן read the same word that רבי יהודה relied on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use אכילה to make someone liable for eating one כזית of a large nerve.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source for eating part of the nerve
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns liability for part of the nerve from the words 'אשר על כף הירך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He learns it from 'that is upon the spoon of the thigh'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that eating part of a big nerve makes you liable. His 'eating' was already used for the כזית minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses the phrase 'that is upon the spoon of the thigh'. It points to only a portion of the nerve, the part on the כף. That shows that eating a portion is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'spoon' of the thigh, a rounded, spoon-shaped mound of flesh on the hip

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מֵ״אֲשֶׁר עַל כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ״ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? He derives it from 'that is upon the spoon of the thigh.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, בראשית 32:33. 'It' is the rule about eating one כזית of a big nerve.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מֵאֲשֶׁר עַל כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי יהודה used אכילה for the כזית minimum, the גמרא finds him another source for רבנן's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns liability for a partial piece from 'אשר על כף הירך'.

steps.title: רבנן use 'upon the spoon' for שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבנן need 'אשר על כף הירך' for שמואל's rule: only the part of the nerve on the כף is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? They need that phrase for שמואל's teaching, for שמואל said: the Torah forbade only the part on the spoon of the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with 'upon the spoon of the thigh'. It answers that they need it for שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that by Torah law only the section of the nerve lying on the כף is forbidden. So רבנן cannot use this phrase to teach about eating part of the nerve. They do not need to, because they already learned that from 'eating'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That phrase is needed for Shmuel's teaching,
as Shmuel said: The Torah prohibited only
the part that is on the spoon of the thigh.
phrases.notes: He means the section of the nerve lying on that spoon-shaped mound, not the rest of the nerve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבנן use the phrase that רבי יהודה just used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use 'אשר על כף הירך' to teach שמואל's rule limiting the איסור to the part on the כף.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the whole thigh is included
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads 'הירך' as including the nerve along the entire thigh, so he does not hold like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? 'The thigh' is written, meaning the whole thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה does not accept שמואל's limit. The פסוק says 'the thigh', and that means all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the word 'הירך' widens the איסור to the nerve along the entire thigh, not just the part on the כף. So the phrase 'על כף' is free for him to use for the partial-eating rule.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? 'The thigh' is written,
meaning the nerve of the entire thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יהודה deals with שמואל's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds that the nerve of the entire thigh is forbidden, based on 'הירך'.

steps.title: רבנן: 'the thigh' excludes the outer nerve
steps.stepSummary: רבנן use 'הירך' to point to the inner nerve, which runs the whole thigh, and to exclude the outer nerve. Even so, only the part on the כף is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? 'The thigh' points to the nerve whose spread covers the whole thigh, to exclude the outer nerve, which is not forbidden. But really only the part on the spoon is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבנן learn from 'the thigh'. It identifies which nerve is meant: the inner one that runs through the whole thigh, and not the outer one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, 'הירך' does not make the whole length of the nerve forbidden. It only tells us which nerve the Torah means: the inner nerve, which spreads through the entire thigh. It leaves out the outer nerve, which is not forbidden by the Torah. Within the inner nerve, they still keep שמואל's rule that only the part on the כף is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer nerve, which is not forbidden by the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Each side uses the פסוק's words differently. רבי יהודה: אכילה means a כזית is needed; על כף means a partial piece counts; הירך means the whole thigh's nerve is forbidden. רבנן: אכילה means a full כזית from part of a larger nerve counts; על כף gives שמואל's limit; הירך means the inner nerve, not the outer one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבנן are contradicting themselves. 'Whole thigh' only identifies which nerve is meant (the inner one). The actual איסור is still only the part on the כף.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That word teaches that it is the nerve that spreads
its prohibition throughout the entire thigh,
phrases.notes: This is the inner nerve, which runs through the whole thigh.

phrases.english: to exclude the outer nerve, which is not forbidden,
but in fact, only the part on the spoon is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַהוּא דְּפָשֵׁיט אִיסּוּרֵיהּ בְּכוּלַּיהּ יָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבנן read the word 'הירך' that רבי יהודה used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use 'הירך' to identify the inner nerve and exclude the outer one, while keeping the איסור limited to the part on the כף.

steps.title: The word כף is already needed to exclude a bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבנן: the word כף is needed to teach that a bird has no גיד הנשה prohibition, so how can it also teach שמואל's rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word 'כף' is needed to exclude a bird, which has no כף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבנן used the word כף in step 4. That word already has a different job: teaching that birds are not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה taught that the גיד הנשה rule does not apply to birds, because a bird's thigh has no rounded כף. If the word כף is used up for that rule, it seems there is nothing left to teach שמואל's rule that only the part on the כף is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'spoon'; the rounded, spoon-shaped part of the thigh bone
To exclude; to teach that something is not included

phrases.english: But this word "כף" is needed
to exclude a bird, which has no כף!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבנן's use of כף for שמואל's rule, which was set up in steps 4 and 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן's reading of 'על כף הירך' as the source for שמואל's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word normally teaches one rule. כף is already used to exclude birds, so it cannot also teach שמואל's rule.

steps.title: The word כף is written twice
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that כף appears twice in the פסוק. One teaches that birds are excluded, and the other teaches שמואל's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק says כף two times, so there is enough wording for both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra mention of כף lets each word carry its own lesson. One excludes birds, which have no כף, and the other limits the prohibition to the part of the nerve on the כף, as שמואל said.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבנן, the word כף appears twice in the פסוק. One mention excludes birds, and the other teaches that only the part of the nerve on the כף is forbidden.

phrases.english: Two "כף"s are written.
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:33 says both 'על כף הירך' and 'בכף ירך יעקב'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought כף appears only once, so it could teach only one rule
steps.terutzMaskana: כף appears twice, so it teaches both that birds are excluded and שמואל's rule

steps.title: A thigh cooked with its גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a thigh cooked with the גיד הנשה inside is forbidden if the nerve gives off enough taste. We measure this as if the nerve were meat cooked with a turnip.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A thigh that was cooked with the גיד הנשה in it, if the nerve can give off taste to it, the thigh is forbidden. How do we measure it? Like meat in a turnip.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens to the meat of a thigh that was cooked with the forbidden nerve still inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is נותן טעם: the thigh is forbidden only if the nerve is big enough to flavor it. To measure this, we picture the nerve as a piece of meat and the thigh as a turnip, and ask whether that much meat would flavor that much turnip.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Gives off taste; the forbidden item is strong enough to flavor the mixture

phrases.english: MISHNA
A thigh that was cooked with the sciatic nerve in it,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם – הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: if there is enough in it to give off taste, it is forbidden.
How do we measure it?
Like meat in a turnip.
phrases.notes: Picture the nerve as a piece of meat and the thigh as a turnip of the same size. Would that meat flavor that turnip?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; opens a new topic about mixtures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thigh cooked with the גיד הנשה is forbidden if the nerve gives off taste, measured like meat flavoring a turnip

steps.title: A גיד הנשה cooked with other sinews
steps.stepSummary: If the גיד הנשה is cooked with other sinews and can be identified, the others are forbidden only if it flavored them. If it cannot be identified, all the sinews are forbidden. The broth is judged by taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גיד הנשה cooked with other sinews: when he recognizes it, the rule is נותן טעם. If not, all of them are forbidden, and the broth goes by נותן טעם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case: the forbidden nerve got mixed into a pot of other sinews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we can pick out the forbidden nerve and remove it, we only check whether it flavored the rest. If we cannot tell which one it is, every sinew is forbidden, since any one of them might be the גיד הנשה. The broth contains no actual piece of the nerve, so it is forbidden only if it picked up enough taste.

keyTerms.meaning: He recognizes it; he can tell which one is the forbidden piece

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. 'כולן אסורין' is about the pieces themselves when the forbidden one cannot be found. The broth is still judged only by taste.

phrases.english: A sciatic nerve that was cooked with the other sinews,
when he recognizes it, the rule is whether it gives off taste,
and if not, all of them are forbidden,
and the broth is judged by whether it gives off taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second mixture case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the nerve is recognized, the rule is נותן טעם. If not, all the sinews are forbidden. The broth is always judged by נותן טעם.

steps.title: The same rule for נבלה and non-kosher fish
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same rule to a piece of נבלה or a piece of non-kosher fish cooked with other pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same for a piece of נבלה, and the same for a piece of non-kosher fish, that was cooked with other pieces: when he recognizes them, the rule is נותן טעם. If not, all of them are forbidden, and the broth goes by נותן טעם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends the rule it just taught about the גיד הנשה to other forbidden foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not special to the גיד הנשה. Any forbidden piece mixed among similar permitted pieces follows the same pattern. If it can be found and removed, we go by taste. If it cannot, all the pieces are forbidden, while the broth still goes by taste.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: Forbidden piece mixed with permitted pieces: if you can find and remove it, check whether it gave off taste. If you cannot, all the pieces are forbidden. The broth is always judged by נותן טעם.

phrases.english: And similarly, a piece of an animal carcass,
and similarly, a piece of non-kosher fish
that was cooked with the other pieces,
when he recognizes them, the rule is whether it gives off taste,
and if not, all of them are forbidden,
and the broth is judged by whether it gives off taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 10 to נבלה and non-kosher fish
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden pieces of נבלה or non-kosher fish mixed with permitted pieces follow the same rule as the גיד הנשה

steps.title: שמואל: roasting does not spread the taste of the nerve
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה: only a thigh cooked with the גיד הנשה is affected by its taste. If it was roasted, one peels and eats the meat until reaching the nerve.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The משנה only taught this rule when the thigh was cooked with the nerve inside it. But if it was roasted with the nerve inside, a person may peel off the meat and eat until he reaches the nerve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה from Step 9. שמואל says that rule only applies to cooking, not to roasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking happens in liquid, so the taste of the nerve spreads through the whole thigh. שמואל holds that when the thigh is roasted, the nerve's taste does not travel through the meat. So one can eat the outer meat and stop only when reaching the nerve itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of… (a way of limiting a משנה)
Peels and eats: cuts away layers of meat and eats them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל is arguing with the משנה. He agrees with it about cooking. He is only saying the משנה's rule does not cover roasting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key question for the סוגיא: does roasting spread forbidden taste the way cooking does?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel said:
They only taught this when it was cooked with it inside,
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה's rule that the thigh is forbidden if the nerve gives it taste.

phrases.english: but if it was roasted with it inside,
he peels off the meat and eats
until he reaches the nerve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְבַּשֵּׁל בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה in Step 9 by limiting its rule to cooking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thigh roasted with the גיד הנשה is not forbidden because of the nerve's taste. One may peel and eat the meat up to the nerve.

steps.title: Challenge from רב הונא: a kid roasted with its fat is fully forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can say roasting does not spread taste, when רב הונא rules that a kid roasted with its forbidden fat is forbidden even at the tip of its ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב הונא said: A young goat that was roasted with its forbidden fat may not be eaten, even from the top of its ear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling from Step 12 by quoting רב הונא, who seems to hold that roasting does spread forbidden taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's case, the forbidden fat (חלב) was roasted with the animal, and the whole animal is forbidden, even the ear, which is far from the fat. That means roasting spreads taste through all the meat. If so, a thigh roasted with the גיד הנשה should also be fully forbidden, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (the גמרא doubting a statement it just heard)
But didn't (so-and-so) say? Brings a source that seems to contradict
Its חלב, the forbidden fat of the animal
The tip of its ear, the part farthest from the fat

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Huna say:
A kid that was roasted with its forbidden fat:
it is forbidden to eat
even from the tip of its ear!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling in Step 12 with a contradicting ruling from רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that roasting with the גיד הנשה does not forbid the whole thigh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא forbids an entire kid roasted with its חלב, even the ear. That shows roasting spreads forbidden taste through all the meat, so a roasted thigh should be fully forbidden too.
